# Rule index

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-rule-index.py from the RFC-0001 sources.
     Do not edit by hand; regenerate with `make rule-index`.
     `make test` fails when this file is stale. -->

Every rule identifier cited in this repository — in code comments, CRD descriptions,
the adapter protocol, conformance output and documentation — is listed here with its
normative statement and the place the specification states it. A public file that
cites an identifier not listed here fails `make test`.

The statements are copied from the specification, not restated. Where a statement
here and the [assembled RFC-0001](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md) differ, the specification
governs.

Bare `R1` … `R4` are admission rules of the resource whose section states them.
They are a different vocabulary from the runtime assertions `RA-n` defined in
[architecture.md](architecture.md).

## Rules stated in RFC-0001

| ID | Rule | Stated in |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **R1 — the discriminator** | `spec.executor` is present if and only if `spec.type` is `External`. An action that sets one without the other is rejected. | [RFC-0001 #fleetaction-external-actions](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetaction-external-actions) |
| **R2 — the forbidden nine** | When `spec.executor` is set, `spec.requiredCapabilities`, `spec.constraints`, `spec.acceptDegradedCapabilities`, `spec.estimatedDurationSeconds`, `spec.robotSelector`, `spec.minBatteryPct`, `spec.preferredRobot`, `spec.preferredManufacturer` and `spec.payload` MUST all be unset. They are forbidden rather than ignored, so a field that could not take effect is refused at apply time instead of silently doing nothing. | [RFC-0001 #fleetaction-external-actions](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetaction-external-actions) |
| **R3 — the `customType` discriminator** | `spec.customType` is accepted if and only if `spec.type` is `Custom`. Setting it beside a named verb is REJECTED, not ignored — the field is a printer column, and a `Navigate` action advertising `customType: clean` would print a claim its own type contradicts. The mirror rule is deliberately absent: `customType` is NOT required when `type` is `Custom`, because requiring it would tighten validation on a published CRD and reject, on their next update, every `Custom` action already in the field. R3 can only ever refuse a field-value pair that no stored object carries, so it is additive. The mirror rule is not added within `swarmada.io/v1` either, for the same reason ([RFC-0001 #resource-model](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#resource-model)). | [RFC-0001 #fleetaction-schema](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetaction-schema) |
| **R4 — the fail-closed pin** | `status.outcomeCertainty: Unestablished` is accepted only alongside `status.phase: Failed`. It is a CEL rule on `status`, so it binds every writer — the reconciler, a raw status patch, a downgraded controller — and an outcome nobody could establish therefore CANNOT be recorded on `Succeeded`, `Cancelled` or a non-terminal phase. The one failure mode that matters for this field is a consumer reading an unestablished outcome as a success; R4 removes it from the schema rather than asking each reader to handle it. A CRD's CEL rules apply to the whole object regardless of which subresource wrote it, which is what makes a rule on `status` enforceable at all. | [RFC-0001 #fleetaction-state-machine](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetaction-state-machine) |
| **FZ-C1** | (*Specified, not implemented at v0.4*: the `FleetZone` admission webhook has no check for either half of this rule, and a CEL rule on one object cannot see another zone's `spec.parentZone`. A zone with child zones may declare members, and a `spec.parentZone` may name a composite; both writes are accepted.) A zone MUST NOT be both a containment parent and a composite. Admission rejects `spec.memberZones` on a zone that has child zones, and rejects a `spec.parentZone` pointing at a composite. Every zone is therefore exactly one of: containment parent, composite, or terminal. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion) |
| **FZ-C2** | `Robot.spec.zone` MUST name a **terminal** zone. This restates the existing leaf-zone invariant over the wider graph: a composite is never a leaf, and a robot is never *in* a composite. `FleetAction.spec.zone` and `ZoneMaintenance.spec.scope.zoneName` MAY name any zone — terminal, containment parent, or composite — and are expanded. (*Partly implemented at v0.4*: the Robot admission gate rejects a `spec.zone` that has child zones, and one with a non-empty `spec.memberZones` on create and on an update that changes `spec.zone`. It does not re-test members on any other update. No `FleetZone` check refuses a child zone created under a zone that a `Robot` declares, or a `spec.parentZone` change that makes one; that robot's zone is then no longer terminal. The `FleetZone` webhook refuses `spec.memberZones` added to a zone that a `Robot` declares, naming the robots; a robot can still declare a composite if it was admitted before that rule, or if the two writes were admitted concurrently, and then FZ-G5 places it in the composite (a composite is never `Containment`) and a per-robot or namespace-scope estop is what reaches it. The member test is not repeated on every update because it would then refuse that robot's per-robot estop as well. `ZoneMaintenance.spec.scope.zoneName` is expanded through members; `FleetAction.spec.zone` is expanded through containment edges only.) | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion) |
| **FZ-C3** | Expansion MUST terminate, MUST deduplicate, and MUST bound depth at 8 composition edges. Containment edges are bounded by the 64-ancestor limit of [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-zone-hierarchy-invariants-controller-enforced](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-zone-hierarchy-invariants-controller-enforced). Cycles across either relation are rejected at admission (as containment cycles already are) and MUST additionally be broken defensively at runtime, because admission cannot see a cycle completed by a resource created concurrently. (*At v0.4*: admission rejects `spec.parentZone` cycles only; composition cycles, self-reference and the 8-edge bound are not checked at admission. `ZoneMaintenance` scope resolution is the one runtime expansion: it breaks a cycle per path, stops past 8 edges, and reports `Cycle` or `DepthExceeded` for the member concerned.) | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion) |
| **FZ-C4** | (*Enforced at v0.4, by the CRD rather than the webhook*: a CEL validation rule on the `FleetZone` spec rejects a non-empty `spec.sharedResources` alongside a non-empty `spec.memberZones`, so the API server refuses the write with a schema error before any admission webhook is called. The traversal half holds: estop propagation follows `spec.parentZone` only. Shared-resource resolution is the namespace-wide scan of [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-sharedresource-types-and-reservation-policy](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-sharedresource-types-and-reservation-policy), not a containment walk.) Composition edges are traversed for **targeting** and MUST NOT be traversed for **inheritance** or **propagation**. A composite contains no physical space, so a `sharedResources` entry declared on one would be a resource the composite does not contain: under the specified containment walk no robot could reach it, and under the v0.4 namespace-wide lookup ([RFC-0001 #fleetzone-sharedresource-types-and-reservation-policy](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-sharedresource-types-and-reservation-policy)) any robot in the namespace could. Admission therefore rejects a non-empty `spec.sharedResources` on a composite. `estopPolicy` propagation likewise follows containment only. The reason is that composition asserts nothing physical: two zones grouped for scheduling convenience may be at opposite ends of a building, and an emergency in one is not evidence of an emergency in the other. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion) |
| **FZ-C5** | (*Enforced at v0.4 by the `FleetZone` admission webhook*, not by CEL: a create carrying `swarmada.io/estop-triggered`, or an update that adds or re-values it, on a zone with a non-empty `spec.memberZones` is refused as `Forbidden` with the message below. Removing the annotation -- the clear -- is never refused. The refusal holds only while the webhook is installed and reachable. A create carrying the annotation is first authorized for the `estop-trigger` verb, as an update is ([RFC-0001 #security-authorization-swarmada-rbac-roles](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#security-authorization-swarmada-rbac-roles)). The premise below, that a composite holds no robot directly, is what the Robot admission rule of FZ-C2 enforces for a robot's declared zone. No robot is placed in a composite by position (FZ-C6). It does not cover a robot that declares a zone which became a composite before the `FleetZone` webhook refused that change, or through a `Robot` and a membership change admitted concurrently; FZ-G5 places such a robot in the composite by declaration, and it is reached per robot or at namespace scope. An update that adds `spec.memberZones` to a zone carrying `swarmada.io/estop-triggered` is refused as `Forbidden` as well: clear the estop, then add the members.) Because of FZ-C4, an estop targeting a composite zone would stop nothing — a composite holds no robots directly and propagates to no members. A silent no-op stop is a false assurance of the most dangerous kind, so the estop path MUST reject it rather than accept it: annotating a composite zone with `swarmada.io/estop-triggered` is rejected at admission with `"FleetZone '<name>' is a composite zone; estop does not propagate across composition edges. Trigger estop on a containment zone, on each member ([<members>]), or at namespace scope."` To stop a floor, target the containment root that physically contains it, or use namespace scope ([RFC-0001 #safety-estop-scopes](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#safety-estop-scopes)). | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion) |
| **FZ-C6** | (*Implemented at v0.4*: the `maxConcurrentRobots` rejection is a CEL validation rule on the `FleetZone` spec, enforced by the API server. The containment half is enforced by the Zone Controller: a zone with a non-empty `spec.memberZones` has `status.geometry.state: Absent` whatever polygon it carries, so it is never a containment candidate and no robot's `currentZone` is derived to it by position. `status.robotCount` counts the containment subtree only.) A composite MAY carry `spec.physicalBounds` as a declared envelope for rendering, and it MUST NOT be used for containment: a robot's `currentZone` is always a terminal zone. Admission rejects a non-zero `spec.maxConcurrentRobots` on a composite for the same reason — capacity is enforced where robots are. `status.robotCount` does not sum a composite's members (see above). | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion) |
| **FZ-G1** | A `FleetZone` MUST be valid with identity alone. `metadata.name` (plus `metadata.namespace`) is the only required content; `spec.physicalBounds` MAY be absent entirely. No consumer, controller, admission check, or adapter MAY reject a `FleetZone`, refuse to target it, or omit it from a listing solely because it carries no geometry. A zone in this state is an **identity-only zone**. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones) |
| **FZ-G2** | (*specified, not implemented at v0.4*: `spec.physicalBounds.frame.id` is in the schema and round-trips, but the FleetZone admission webhook has no frame check, so a polygon declaring no frame is accepted. An absent frame is read as `SiteAligned` with an empty id.) When `spec.physicalBounds.polygon` is set, `spec.physicalBounds.frame.id` MUST be set. A polygon without a declared frame is rejected at admission. Coordinates with no stated frame are not geometry; they are numbers. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones) |
| **FZ-G3** | The control plane MUST NOT transform coordinates between frames, consistent with the namespace-level rule in [RFC-0001 #swarmadaconfig-coordinate-system](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#swarmadaconfig-coordinate-system). Only a polygon whose `frame.alignment` is `SiteAligned` — meaning its vertices are directly comparable with `Robot.status.position` and the edge `PositionFrame` stream in the frame `SwarmadaConfig.spec.coordinateSystem` declares — participates in containment. A polygon declared `FrameLocal` MUST NOT be used for containment derivation, boundary-breach detection, or overlap arbitration; it is carried for consumers that know how to place it (visualization, an operator import tool, an adapter that owns the transform) and for nothing else. Whoever writes the polygon, an operator or an import tool acting for one, MUST declare `FrameLocal` when it cannot vouch for site alignment (a Fleet Adapter writes no `FleetZone`); a wrong `SiteAligned` claim produces silently wrong containment, which is worse than no geometry. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones) |
| **FZ-G4** | The Zone Controller MUST skip a zone whose geometry state, computed from its `spec.physicalBounds` and never read back from `status.geometry`, is not `Containment` when deriving `Robot.status.currentZone` from position ([RFC-0001 #fleetzone-zone-controller-current-zone-derivation](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-zone-controller-current-zone-derivation)). It MUST NOT treat such a zone as covering no space (which would make every robot in it unmatched) nor as covering all space (which would match every robot in the namespace). It covers unknown space, and the derivation has nothing to say about it. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones) |
| **FZ-G5** | **Membership in an identity-only zone is declared, not derived.** For a robot whose `spec.zone` names a zone with `status.geometry.state != Containment`, the Zone Controller MUST set `status.currentZone` to that zone name, MUST set `status.specZoneMatchesCurrent: true`, and MUST NOT emit `ZonePositionUnmatched` for that robot. The operator's (or the adapter's) assignment is the authority on where the robot is, because nothing else in the control plane is in a position to contradict it. The cost is stated plainly in FZ-G7. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones) |
| **FZ-G6** | Every identity-scoped behaviour of a `FleetZone` MUST behave identically whether or not geometry is present: `maxConcurrentRobots` capacity enforcement, TDE reservations and shared-resource queues ([RFC-0001 #tde](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#tde)), shared-resource name lookup ([RFC-0001 #fleetzone-sharedresource-types-and-reservation-policy](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-sharedresource-types-and-reservation-policy)), `estopPolicy` propagation, `ZoneMaintenance` scoping, RBAC, and zone expansion ([RFC-0001 #fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-composite-zones-and-zone-expansion)). None of these reads a polygon. A fleet of identity-only zones is fully schedulable, fully stoppable, and fully deconflicted. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones) |
| **FZ-G7** | Every geometry-derived behaviour MUST degrade **explicitly**, never silently. The Zone Controller MUST publish a `GeometryAvailable` condition on the zone, `False` with reason `IdentityOnly` (no polygon), `FrameLocalGeometry` (polygon present, not site-aligned) or `CompositeZone` (a composite, whose polygon is never used for containment, FZ-C6). While that condition is `False`: the control plane MUST NOT claim zone-boundary-breach detection for the zone, and an edge node serving it MUST NOT report the zone as geofenced — the edge trigger table in [RFC-0001 #safety-edge-headless-emergency-stop](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#safety-edge-headless-emergency-stop) evaluates cached zone polygons, and there are none to cache. The reference edge node caches a zone's polygon only when the zone's geometry state is `Containment`, the same classification the Zone Controller writes to `status.geometry`, so a `FrameLocal` zone and a composite are never geofenced, and a robot whose `spec.zone` names one is not evaluated for a boundary breach. A robot may leave an identity-only zone physically and the control plane will not know: `currentZone` continues to read the declared value (FZ-G5) because the alternative is to withhold work from every robot on a platform that cannot export a map. Operators MUST NOT treat an identity-only zone as a containment boundary for personnel-safety purposes; the hardware safety layer of [RFC-0001 #safety-scope-and-responsibility-boundary](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#safety-scope-and-responsibility-boundary) is unaffected by any of this and remains the only thing that was ever load-bearing for personnel. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones) |
| **FZ-G8** | Mixed namespaces are expected and legal. A namespace MAY contain identity-only zones, site-aligned zones, and frame-local zones simultaneously, and the mix MAY change over time as an adapter gains or loses the ability to export a map. Adding geometry to an identity-only zone is a widening change: derivation begins to apply, and a robot whose declared zone no longer matches its reported position becomes visible as unmatched. Implementations MUST tolerate this transition without disturbing in-flight actions ([RFC-0001 #fleetzone-zone-controller-current-zone-derivation](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-zone-controller-current-zone-derivation), "Between-zone positions"). A robot placed by declaration that has sent no position frame keeps its declared `currentZone` through the widening, and is reported by the `ZonePositionOverdue` condition ([RFC-0001 #fleetzone-zone-controller-current-zone-derivation](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-zone-controller-current-zone-derivation), "Robots that report no position"). | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-optional-geometry-and-identity-only-zones) |
| **FZ-Z1** | A zone's extent is the planar region enclosed by `spec.physicalBounds.polygon`, qualified by the discrete `spec.physicalBounds.floor`. Containment is a point-in-polygon test on `x`/`y` plus **exact `floor` equality, in every namespace**. `floor` and `polygon` are both required whenever `spec.physicalBounds` is present -- neither carries `+optional`, so the generated CRD demands both -- and the containment derivation applies the `floor` filter unconditionally, with no `Geodetic` branch. A `Geodetic` namespace therefore does not exempt a zone from `floor`: the test is point-in-polygon on longitude/latitude **and** `floor` equality, and a position whose `floor` differs from the zone's matches nothing. A geodetic deployment MUST agree one `floor` convention across its zones and the positions its adapters report; `0` is the obvious choice, and a zone left at a different value is silently unmatchable rather than loosely matched. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-zone-extent-is-two-dimensional](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-zone-extent-is-two-dimensional) |
| **FZ-Z2** | Altitude MUST NOT be an input to containment. `spec.physicalBounds.minAltitude` and `maxAltitude` are a **declared geofence bound** for adapters and edge nodes to enforce on the far side of the interop boundary — they are not a containment test, not a capacity dimension, and not an arbitration input, and no control-plane decision reads them. (At v0.4 they are additionally never transmitted, so the ceiling is enforced nowhere; see the Maturity note.) | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-zone-extent-is-two-dimensional](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-zone-extent-is-two-dimensional) |
| **FZ-Z3** | Altitude MUST NOT be an input to arbitration. Zone capacity (`maxConcurrentRobots`), TDE reservations, shared-resource queues, estop scope, and `ZoneMaintenance` scope all operate on zone membership, and zone membership is two-dimensional. Two robots in the same zone contend, whatever their vertical separation. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-zone-extent-is-two-dimensional](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-zone-extent-is-two-dimensional) |
| **FZ-Z4** | `floor` is a discrete label, not a coordinate. Floors do not overlap, are not ordered for any geometric purpose, and MUST NOT be interpolated: there is no "between floor 2 and floor 3". A drone flying up a two-storey atrium is on exactly one `floor` value at a time, whichever its adapter reports. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-zone-extent-is-two-dimensional](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-zone-extent-is-two-dimensional) |
| **FZ-Z5** | A `FleetZone` carries no domain discriminator. There is no `Ground`/`Aerial` field, and a zone MUST NOT be interpreted as belonging to one domain or the other. Any two robots admitted to the same zone are peers as far as this specification is concerned. | [RFC-0001 #fleetzone-zone-extent-is-two-dimensional](../rfcs/dist/RFC-0001-core-spec.md#fleetzone-zone-extent-is-two-dimensional) |

## Rules staged for RFC-0001

These rules are amendments to RFC-0001 that its assembled text does not contain.
This index is where they are published.

### Zone Exclusions — an excluded region is a child zone whose entry restriction is Denied

Status: accepted (ADR-0069).

| ID | Rule |
| :---- | :---- |
| **FZ-X1** | An excluded region MUST be expressed as a `FleetZone` whose `spec.parentZone` names the zone the region is cut out of, whose `spec.physicalBounds` covers the excluded region on the same `floor` and in the same frame as its parent, and whose `spec.restrictions.entry.mode` is `Denied`. The containment relation is `spec.parentZone`; `spec.memberZones` MUST NOT be used, because composition asserts nothing physical (FZ-C4) and is not traversed by the restriction fold (FZ-R1). |
| **FZ-X2** | Containment is a **set**, so a robot inside an excluded region is contained by the parent **and** the exclusion simultaneously, and both appear in `Robot.status.containingZones[]` (FZ-R10). Restrictions aggregate over that set and `Denied` absorbs (FZ-R2), so the robot is bound by the denial whatever else contains it. |
| **FZ-X3** | An action targeting the exclusion is refused **terminally**, with `status.failureReason: ZoneEntryDenied`, by candidate filter 11. An action targeting an ancestor has the exclusion **removed from its resolved leaf set and named** in the narrowed-out report — the whole floor is not refused for one excluded pillar, and the pillar is not dropped silently. Both behaviours are candidate filter 11's, unchanged: *absorbing over the target relation, narrowing over the subtree*, with the narrowed leaf set reported and never silent. An exclusion is a denied descendant like any other. |
| **FZ-X4** | **The zone that carries exclusion children MUST NOT be the zone robots occupy.** The navigable remainder MUST be its own sibling child of the same parent. A leaf set is resolved by walking the containment tree **downward to zones with no children**, so a zone that gains an exclusion child is no longer in its own leaf set: its open area then belongs to no leaf, candidate filter 2 excludes every robot reporting the parent as `status.currentZone`, and — once every remaining leaf is denied — filter 11 refuses the action terminally with *"the subtree is exhausted"*. The refusal is fail-closed and is still a floor-wide outage. The conforming shape is three objects: a container, a navigable remainder, and one exclusion per region. |
| **FZ-X5** | **An exclusion does not make a region protected.** A control-plane refusal means the action was **not dispatched**; it is not a claim that no robot enters the region. Nothing in this specification reaches a robot driven by its own vendor application, its own buttons or its own schedule, and entry restrictions are **not** carried on the adapter wire — only the operating axis is (FA-R7). An operator surface that reports an exclusion as *protected* rather than as *not dispatched to* claims a property this API does not provide. |
| **FZ-X6** | A robot already inside a region when its denial takes effect is governed by `spec.restrictions.entry.occupantAction`, unchanged: `Report` is the default and the only value implemented, **no robot is moved**, and one `ZoneEntryDeniedWithOccupants` Warning names who was inside. Withholding new work is credited to the denial, not to this field. |

### Zone Restrictions — entry, capability and operating constraints on FleetZone

Status: accepted (ADR-0058).

| ID | Rule |
| :---- | :---- |
| **FA-R1 — declare** | An adapter MUST declare, in `CapabilitiesSnapshot.honoured_operating_constraints` (additive; a new field number in `fleet_adapter.v1`), the operating subjects it can honour for each robot. The control plane projects it read-only to `Robot.status.honouredOperatingConstraints[]`, the same path `sensor_streams` already takes. An adapter that declares none is not in breach; its robots are withheld from zones that restrict a subject (RFC-0001 Control Plane, *Scheduler*, filter 12). |
| **FA-R2 — carry** | The control plane MUST send, on `AssignAction` (additive; a new field number), the **resolved effective** operating rules in force **at the zone the robot is being dispatched to, folded per FZ-R11 with every zone of its `status.containingZones[]`** — its `status.currentZone`, which candidate filter 2 has already proven is within the resolved leaf set of `spec.zone`, or, for a pinned robot standing outside that set, the **target's own chain** — in each case the same set filter 12 judged that robot against. The adapter is never asked to walk a zone tree, and never receives a rule that resolution has already superseded. **The scope is the leaf, not the target's own chain** (RFC-0001 Control Plane, *Scheduler*, filter 12): filter 2 admits robots from the whole subtree, so the target's own projection is empty for an action on a zone whose rule is declared one level down, and an adapter sent that set has nothing to decline. The leaf's projection already contains every ancestor's rule, the target's included, so this is narrower in scope and never narrower in content. |
| **FA-R3 — honour** | An adapter that accepts an assignment carrying an operating rule MUST honour it for the whole time the robot is in the zone, including while only passing through: the rule constrains the robot's **state**, not the action. |
| **FA-R4 — attest** | **WITHDRAWN from this contract — see *Why FA-R4 is withdrawn rather than given a field* below.** The withdrawn text required the adapter to report, on the action's terminal outcome, which subjects it honoured. There is nowhere on the wire for the report to go, nowhere in the control plane for it to be recorded, and nothing that would read it; an obligation in that position has already stopped being one. This contract carries no attestation obligation; the shape one would take is stated below so it is not re-derived. **An attestation is a claim, not a measurement** — that half of the original text is unaffected and is why the obligation was never verifiable in the first place. |
| **FA-R5 — decline** | An adapter that **cannot** honour a rule MUST decline the assignment — `AssignActionRejection` gains a value for it, and `AssignActionResult` carries the subjects it could not honour — rather than accepting it and ignoring the rule. Declining costs the adapter nothing: row A24 of RFC-0001's action table applies and the Scheduler tries the next candidate. |
| **FA-R6 — unknown means decline** | An adapter that receives a rule whose `subject` it does not recognise MUST decline under FA-R5 naming that subject. An unrecognised constraint is **not** an absent constraint; treating it as absent would make the namespaced extension form a universal bypass. |
| **FA-R7 — tell, continuously** | The control plane MUST send the resolved operating rules in force **across every zone containing the robot** on a `zone_constraints` Command, when that answer changes, and again to each robot that stands in a zone when its adapter registers a `ControlStream`, because a newly connected adapter process holds no rule set; it sends them at no other time. It is **what makes FA-R3 satisfiable** and adds no honour obligation of its own (its adapter rules govern whether an adapter must implement the push and how it reads one): FA-R3 already binds an adapter for the whole time the robot is in the zone, including while transiting, and `AssignAction` only ever carried the rules in force where the robot stood at dispatch, once — so an adapter entering any other zone had no rule set for where it was. `Denied`, `Limited` **and `Required`** all travel: entering a zone can oblige a subject to be **on**. An **empty** set with no `unresolved_zones` means no rule is in force in any zone whose site-aligned polygon contains the robot, which is permission for those zones, and is how the plane says a robot has LEFT a restricted region; an adapter MUST NOT read it as a lockout. A push never revokes the rules carried on the robot's current `AssignAction`: FA-R3 still binds them, including in a zone FZ-R12 keeps out of `containingZones[]`. The command is **optional** for an adapter that declares no subject under FA-R1: such an adapter answers `unsupported=true` and is not in breach. An adapter that declares any subject MUST implement it, since without it the transit half of FA-R3 cannot be met. **THE RULE ARRIVES AFTER THE ROBOT CROSSES THE BOUNDARY** — the loop is telemetry-up then command-down — so this does not make a zone safe, and no implementation or operator surface may present it as doing so (ADR-0059 §6). |
| **FZ-R1** | For each *(axis, subject)*, the **effective** rule for a zone is the most restrictive rule declared anywhere in its ancestor chain, root-downward, including the zone itself. `Denied` is more restrictive than `Limited`, which is more restrictive than no rule. Between two `Limited` rules on one subject the **tighter** `max` wins and the **intersection** of the `allowed` lists wins. Between `Required` and `Limited` on one subject the effective rule is `Required` and it keeps the bound: the tighter `max`, or the intersection of the `allowed` lists. The pair is not a contradiction (only `Denied` with `Required` is, FZ-R3), and the order in the chain does not change the answer. A nearest-ancestor-wins resolution does not conform. |
| **FZ-R2** | Denial is **absorbing**. No resolution, merge, or default may produce an effective rule more permissive than a rule declared by an ancestor. An implementation whose resolver can emit a weaker effective rule than some rule it read does not conform, whatever its admission checks do. |
| **FZ-R3** | `Denied` and `Required` on the same subject in one chain are a **contradiction**, not a widening. It resolves to `Denied`, and the zone publishes `RestrictionsConsistent: False` naming both declaring zones plus a `RestrictionContradiction` Warning event. `Denied` wins because a zone in which a camera must be off and must be on is a zone no robot may work in; resolving the other way would switch a camera on in a patient room by operation of a merge rule. |
| **FZ-R4** | The Zone Controller writes the resolved set to `status.restrictions.effective[]`, each entry naming the zone it was `inheritedFrom`, and publishes `RestrictionsResolved`. **Consumers read `status`, never the tree**, for the same reason they read `status.geometry` rather than inspecting `spec.physicalBounds`: "what is forbidden here" is decided in one place. |
| **FZ-R5** | `status.restrictions` is a projection of `spec` and the zone tree. It MUST be recomputed on a spec or topology change and MUST NOT be recomputed on a telemetry tick; it carries no per-robot and no positional data. Restriction handling adds **no new per-tick status write anywhere** in this specification. |
| **FZ-R6** | Resolution MUST fail **closed**. A zone whose ancestor chain cannot be read, or that names a `parentZone` that does not resolve, publishes `RestrictionsResolved: False` and is treated as **not dispatchable** until it resolves. An unresolvable restriction is not an absent restriction. |
| **FZ-R7** | A write that makes a **descendant** more permissive than an ancestor — a raised `max`, a widened `allowed` list, a `Required` under an ancestor's `Denied` or the reverse — is **rejected at admission**, naming the ancestor zone and the conflicting rule. It is never silently ignored: silently ignoring produces an object whose `spec` says one thing and whose behaviour is another, and the purpose of this surface is that the API is where the rule is stated. |
| **FZ-R8** | A write that makes an **ancestor** more restrictive is **always admitted**, even when an existing descendant now contradicts it. The contradiction resolves per FZ-R1/FZ-R3 and is reported on the descendant (`RestrictionsConsistent: False` plus a Warning event). Refusing a parent's tightening on account of a child would make a boundary un-addable, would let a leaf veto a site policy, and would require the webhook to list a whole subtree on every zone write. |
| **FZ-R9** | **Admission is the diagnostic; resolution is the enforcement.** FZ-R7 tells an operator now; FZ-R1–FZ-R2 hold on an object admission never saw — restored from a backup, applied before the webhook was installed, written under `failurePolicy: Ignore`, or raced past the check. An implementation that enforces FZ-R7 and resolves nearest-ancestor-wins has built the diagnostic and skipped the invariant. |
| **FZ-R10** | **Containment is a SET, and restrictions aggregate over it.** A robot is subject to the effective restrictions of **every zone whose polygon contains it**, not only the one arbitrated onto `Robot.status.currentZone`. Zone polygons may overlap, and `currentZone` resolves an overlap to one winner to answer *where the robot reports it is*; using that winner to decide *what binds it* discards the loser's rules, which is the permissive direction and does not conform. The set is published on `Robot.status.containingZones[]`, sorted, and `currentZone` keeps its cardinality and its derivation unchanged. |
| **FZ-R11** | **The aggregate is a UNION OF ALREADY-RESOLVED PROJECTIONS, then the ordinary most-restrictive fold.** Each containing zone's `status.restrictions.effective[]` has already folded that zone's own ancestor chain (FZ-R1/FZ-R4); the union folds those answers by the same rules — `Denied` absorbs, two `max` values take the tighter, two `allowed` lists intersect, `Denied` plus `Required` resolves to `Denied`. An implementation that re-walks the tree to compute this has built a second resolver, which FZ-R4 forbids; a second resolver can drift from the first, and a nearest-ancestor-wins one does not conform (FZ-R1). `inheritedFrom` survives the union naming the **declaring** zone, never the containing one. |
| **FZ-R12** | **A zone with no site-aligned polygon has no containment answer, and is not a member.** A zone whose geometry state is `Absent` or `FrameLocal` never appears in `containingZones[]`: containment cannot be derived for a region whose shape in the site frame the plane does not know. Robots inside such a zone's declared region are governed by the **assignment path alone** — filters 11 and 12 still evaluate its restrictions for an action that targets it. The condition `GeometryAvailable: False` already reports this per zone and is the place an operator learns it. |
<!-- staged-rules: end -->
